- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates downside risk; increase forecasted lows by 5–10% to account for volatility.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecasted peak by 10–15%.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model shows strong upward trend after 10+ consecutive days of rising prices, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–15% after sentiment drops below 0.0.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid over-reliance on recent 7-day highs; use 14-day moving average as a sanity check to prevent runaway momentum bias.
